events.title: St. Brice's Day Massacre
events.description: King Æthelred II of England ordered the killing of Danes living in England. The order was given on the feast day of St. Brice. It is one of the most notorious acts of his reign.
events.significance: The massacre is said to have provoked Danish retaliation. That retaliation led to Sweyn Forkbeard's invasion and, eventually, Danish rule over England.

events.title: Patriot Forces Occupy Montreal
events.description: During the American Revolutionary War, Continental forces under General Richard Montgomery entered Montreal. The city was lightly defended and fell without a major fight.
events.significance: The capture was the high point of the American invasion of Canada. The campaign ended in failure at Quebec City weeks later.

events.title: Holland Tunnel Opens
events.description: The Holland Tunnel opened to traffic. It was the first vehicular tunnel under the Hudson River, linking New Jersey and New York City.
events.significance: The tunnel was a landmark of civil engineering. It eased the region's dependence on ferries and shaped the commuter patterns of the New York metropolitan area.

events.title: Bhola Cyclone Strikes East Pakistan
events.description: A catastrophic tropical cyclone hit the coast of East Pakistan, now Bangladesh. It killed an estimated 500,000 people.
events.significance: It is among the deadliest tropical cyclones ever recorded. Anger over the government's slow relief response fed the political crisis that led to Bangladesh's independence in 1971.
